links.outcome: Harm discovery by adversarial multi-turn evaluation versus static benchmarks for mental health LLMs
links.effect: Adversarial multi-turn agent-based evaluation revealed substantial role-dependent and cumulative safety failures missed by static benchmarks, and improved failure-mode coverage and diagnostic granularity. No numbers are available in the text provided.
links.quote: Our results reveal substantial role-dependent and cumulative safety failures that are systematically missed by existing static benchmarks, and show that our framework significantly improves failure-mode coverage and diagnostic granularity.

unlisted_practices: Role-aware harm taxonomy (perpetrator, instigator, facilitator, enabler) for classifying AI counselor safety failures
Trajectory-level closed-loop agent-based safety evaluation of multi-turn counseling

screen.reason: The study develops and applies an evaluation benchmark (MHSafeEval) and safety taxonomy (R-MHSafe) to assess LLM safety in multi-turn mental health counseling via simulated adversarial interactions; it does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice implementation.
